reason: B is the stronger proposal because it specifies a controlled, testable powder intervention and is supported by prior demonstration of resonant-acoustic Y2O3 incorporation and strengthening in an L-PBF multi-principal-element alloy. Its residual-stress mechanism remains weak—dispersoids do not directly reduce thermal gradients—but A relies on the more doubtful premise that 900–1000 °C solid-state sintering can fully densify oxidation-prone AlCrFeNiSi while retaining a fine microstructure and improving properties, without supporting evidence.
